question: After this branch is rebased, should maintainers accept the focused runner/Codex regression proof for timed-out Codex app-server lane release, or require live wedge proof before merge?
rationale: The source and regression test support the runner contract, but the user-facing incident involved session state and message delivery under a live Codex/WhatsApp-style stall, which automation cannot waive while the PR is marked for human review.

options.title: Accept Focused Proof After Rebase
options.body: Rebase the branch, preserve current abort handling, rerun required checks, and treat the focused runner regression as sufficient for this lane-release contract.

options.title: Require Live Wedge Proof
options.body: Pause merge until a live or Crabbox Codex app-server wedge shows the lane releases without corrupting session state or channel delivery.

options.title: Close Or Replace
options.body: If maintainers do not want to carry the session-overlap risk, close this replacement and keep the broader production issue open for a different fix shape.

recommendation.title: Accept Focused Proof After Rebase
recommendation.body: Rebase the branch, preserve current abort handling, rerun required checks, and treat the focused runner regression as sufficient for this lane-release contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Best available owner because they merged the adjacent native lane-release contract and were active on the source Codex lane-release review.
